next_steps: Redwood (Ethan) - share full request-level logs and sample traces for incident by 2026-04-09

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-08 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sara (Nova PM), Jorge (Nova SRE), Priya (Nova ML)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to review last week's reliability incident (timeouts / 5xx spike), align on root-cause hypotheses, and agree next steps for pilot stability and telemetry.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off. this is the weekly poc sync, main agenda is follow up on the outage on monday where you saw increased 5xxs and timeouts. Ethan's got the deeper logs. Sara any quick context from product side?
[00:18] Sara: yeah thanks, um the incident surfaced when we pushed a marketing campaign, traffic spiked ~2.5x for about 12 minutes, we started seeing user complaints and our app recorded a lot of aborted calls. Jorge took over ops and saw a bunch of 502/504. Priya is here too for ML side.
[00:36] Ethan: hi all, quick reminder, our pilot is on Redwood Dedicated pool in us-east with k8s autoscale. we observed error types: 502/504, request timeouts at the client, and intermittent rate-limit 429s during the warm-up. logs look like backend worker queue saturation and repeated retries from the client causing a retry storm.
[01:05] Jorge: yeah from Nova's side we had allowed the client lib to retry aggressively — default 3 retries with no jitter — so when the upstream latency climbed, the retries multiplied and we saw effective concurrency spike.
[01:28] Priya: also worth noting our input distribution changed — longer prompts and more embeddings usage — so sequence lengths spiked, which increases token processing time per request.
[01:45] Maya: ok good, so multiple factors: traffic burst, retry storms, sequence length distribution, and possible capacity provisioning gap. Ethan, what does the Redwood runtime show re: KV cache and batching behavior?
[02:05] Ethan: from the traces we have, the KV cache hit rate dropped during the spike because clients were hitting new prefixes; caching helped earlier but the campaign had diverse inputs. Also the continuous batching queue grew, and when we scaled pods the cold-starts for certain kernel paths caused short windows of elevated latency — those manifested as 502s behind our gateway.
[02:37] Sara: sorry can you explain "kernel paths" quick? is that like different quantization or model variants?
[02:45] Ethan: yeah uh so the runtime chooses optimized kernels based on seq len and model config; when we hit a different seq length distribution we sometimes take a fallback codepath until the warm caches populate. it's normal but the combination with autoscaler latency is what bit us.
[03:05] Jorge: were there any 5xxs that looked like upstream infra failures vs. gateway timeouts? we saw some 502s that looked immediate.
[03:17] Ethan: most were downstream gateway timeouts — essentially requests waiting on a busy worker then gateway returning 502/504. Only a handful look like transient infra OOMs which we flagged and hopped the nodes recovered.
[03:35] Priya: on client side we log latency at call boundaries — i can share a chart where p95 jumps from 200ms to ~1.8s during the spike, which triggered our retry logic.
[03:50] Sara: that matches what we saw. users hit retry in the UI and server got more load.

--- Topics: telemetry gaps, retry & client config, autoscale tuning, rate limiting, longer prompt handling, postmortem plan ---

[05:00] Maya: ok concrete items — telemetry: we need request-level traces that tie client request id to Redwood request id. Ethan, can you surface that?
[05:12] Ethan: yes i can dump the request traces. i'm going to attach the full trace set and a condensed csv for the spike window. note, some ids may be obfuscated, but we'll preserve some mapping. i'll upload to the shared doc: link: https://redwood.app/share/incident-logs-2026-04-06.csv
[05:32] Jorge: great. also on our side we'll send the spike traffic pattern — exact timestamps and client retry settings, and the SDK version.

[06:00] Sara: question: what could we change quickly to prevent this repeating, before we do a full root cause fix?
[06:08] Ethan: short term — increase request quotas/rate limits for the pilot so gateway doesn't return 429s at the first sign of spike, add server-side queued request smoothing and apply exponential backoff with jitter at client. We can also pre-warm extra capacity when you expect marketing traffic.
[06:30] Jorge: pre-warm + change client retry is doable. we can add jitter and reduce retries to 1 or 0 for non-critical UX paths.
[06:42] Maya: also we can tweak autoscaler thresholds and reduce scaling step delays. Ethan, can you propose specific autoscale parameters?
[06:50] Ethan: yes propose: reduce target CPU threshold from 70% to 55% for this pool, enable faster scale-up (shorten cooldown from 3m to 60s), and provision a small buffer of burst instances (2-3) so cold-starts don't coincide with spikes.
[07:12] Priya: will that increase cost a lot for pilot?
[07:18] Maya: we can keep burst instances as reserved for specific windows to limit cost; we'll estimate cost impact and share.

[08:00] Jorge: what about caching behavior — can we increase KV cache warmup for common prefixes? our traffic is mostly product lookup prompts with similar prefixes.
[08:12] Ethan: yes we can suggest a cache pre-warm step; Redwood can prepopulate KV cache with top N prefixes if you provide a list of common prompts. also we can bump batch size window to absorb short bursts but that increases per-request latency slightly.
[08:32] Sara: tradeoffs noted: latency vs throughput/cost.

[09:00] Ethan: logs show a pattern of client retries overlapping with autoscaler spin-up; that created a sawtooth effect. adding client jitter and BYO-idempotency key will let the runtime dedupe some work.
[09:20] Priya: we can implement idempotency key for our calls, good idea.

[10:00] Maya: ok near-term mitigations: 1) Nova change client retry logic (reduce retries, add jitter, idempotency). 2) Redwood adjust autoscale and pre-warm strategy. 3) temporary rate limit increase and pilot buffer. 4) share full traces and postmortem doc.

[11:00] Jorge: about the 5xxs that looked like OOMs, do you have logs for the container OOMs? we want to know if it's memory pressure from long sequences.
[11:12] Ethan: yes we pulled container metrics; memory climbed for some pods processing long sequences and occasionally hit high water. we have heap snapshots — i'll include aggregated metrics in the upload.
[11:30] Priya: we recently increased max sequence length in our requests. if we reduce requested max length or trim prompts, that helps too.

[12:00] Sara: what's the recommended client-side default from Redwood for retries and jitter?
[12:10] Ethan: recommended pattern: at most 1 retry, exponential backoff starting at 200ms with full jitter (0-200ms), and avoid retrying on 4xx. add idempotency keys for any non-purely-read call.

[13:00] Maya: let's cover observability gaps — which metrics you want us to expose in the console?
[13:10] Jorge: request latency p50/p95/p99, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, pod start time, prewarm success, number of 5xx per minute, and request id mapping to client id.
[13:30] Ethan: we can add dashboards for those and grant Nova access to a special pilot dashboard. will push a draft dashboard link: https://redwood.app/dashboards/nova-pilot

[15:00] Sara: timeline — we need confidence before next campaign on friday. can we get short-term mitigations in by thursday?
[15:10] Maya: yes we'll prioritize. Ethan will drop traces by tomorrow, Jorge will return client config same day, and we'll schedule the postmortem on tuesday.

[17:00] Ethan: quick note on rate limits — in our gateway the default burst allowance was conservative for new pilots. we can raise it for Nova temporarily and monitor; if you prefer we can also add a soft-rejection where we return 429 but with Retry-After and less aggressive circuit behaviour.
[17:30] Jorge: temporary raise ok, but we want per-route controls. do you support that?
[17:36] Ethan: yes per-route quotas exist; we can set per-project and per-route limits.

[20:00] Maya: ok let's summarize next steps and owners.
[20:05] Maya: Ethan to upload traces and condensed csv (by 2026-04-09). Ethan to propose autoscale params and dashboard updates (by 2026-04-10). Maya to send updated pricing/credits + runbook (by 2026-04-12). Jorge to share client retry config and traffic spike data (by 2026-04-10). Both to schedule postmortem 2026-04-14.

[21:00] Sara: any blockers on Redwood side for prewarming caches? how do we provide prefixes?
[21:10] Ethan: you can drop a list of top 200 prefixes into the shared spreadsheet and we'll run a prewarm job before the campaign.
[21:22] Sara: ok we'll compile that and share.

[22:00] Priya: a few smaller asks — can Redwood add a flag to lower model precision for non-critical calls to reduce mem? even a quantized path for big prompts would help.
[22:14] Ethan: we do have quantized variants; for pilot we can enable a lower-precision variant for certain routes — will propose list of routes and potential quality degradation tradeoffs.

[23:00] Jorge: also can we get request sampling for full audio of the transcript? just kidding — but we want full request + response size histograms.

[24:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links. again links: incident traces: https://redwood.app/share/incident-logs-2026-04-06.csv dashboard draft: https://redwood.app/dashboards/nova-pilot runbook: https://redwood.app/docs/pilot-runbook

[25:00] (cross talk) Sara: thanks, appreciate the quick response. Priya: thanks folks. Ethan: thanks, will upload traces today.
[25:30] Maya: end meeting.

Action items (as discussed):
- Ethan Cole - upload request-level traces + condensed csv for spike window (due 2026-04-09)
- Ethan Cole - propose autoscaler and prewarm params + dashboard changes (due 2026-04-10)
- Maya Patel - share updated pilot credits/pricing and runbook (due 2026-04-12)
- Jorge Alvarez - share client retry configs and exact spike timestamps (due 2026-04-10)
- Priya Nair - provide top prefixes for KV cache prewarm (due 2026-04-11)

Notes: Transcription imperfect in places; proper nouns may be slightly off (kernel paths / k-v cache). References to shared artifacts inserted as links above. Agreed to temporary rate-limit increase + client retry changes and schedule deeper postmortem for 2026-04-14.
